chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who sent someone to propose marriage to a woman on his behalf while he was absent, so they married the absent man, and the dowry was fixed. Then news came that he had died after the dowry had been taken. He said: 'If he acquired ownership after death, she has no dowry and no inheritance. If he acquired ownership before death, she has half the dowry, she is an heir, and she observes the waiting period.'
ai.seo_question: What are the financial and marital rights of a bride if her fiancé dies after the marriage contract but before consummation?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the critical distinction between the conclusion of the marriage contract (nikah) and the actual transfer of ownership (qabd) of the dowry (mahr), a key principle in Shia jurisprudence. It establishes that if the groom died before acquiring the dowry, the marriage is considered incomplete for inheritance purposes, whereas post-acquisition ensures full rights including half the dowry, inheritance, and the iddah period. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the practical realization of contractual obligations over mere verbal agreement in matters of marital finance.
